title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2026/196 of 28 January 2026 amending Regulation (EC) No 1333/2008 of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards the use of carrageenan (E 407), locust bean gum (E 410), guar gum (E 412), gum arabic (acacia gum) (E 414), xanthan gum (E 415), pectins (E 440) and starch sodium octenyl succinate (E 1450) and Commission Regulation (EU) No 231/2012 as regards specifications for locust bean gum (E 410), guar gum (E 412), gum arabic (acacia gum) (E 414), xanthan gum (E 415), pectins (E 440) and starch sodium octenyl succinate (E 1450)
journal: Official Journal of the European Union, L series, 2026/196, 29 January 2026
result: Recital: on 29 January 2021 EFSA concluded that the use of pectins (E 440) in food categories 13.1.5.1 and 13.1.5.2 at the then authorised levels raises health risks. Annex I: in 13.1.5.1 (foods for special medical purposes intended for infants) and 13.1.5.2 (foods for special medical purposes intended for infants from four months and young children), the entry for E 440 pectins becomes 4,000 mg/kg, from birth onwards in products used in case of gastro-intestinal disorders; in 01.10 (milk-based drinks for young children) E 440 is 5,000 mg/kg, lowered proportionally when combined with E 407, E 410, E 412, E 414 or E 415. Annex II, specifications for E 440(i) pectin and E 440(ii) amidated pectin: the final product must not show residual enzyme activity; dispersible in water forming a colloidal, opalescent dispersion; arsenic not more than 0.1 mg/kg; lead not more than 0.3 mg/kg in foods for infants and young children and 1 mg/kg otherwise; mercury not more than 0.1 mg/kg; cadmium not more than 0.1 and 0.5 mg/kg; aluminium not more than 120 and 200 mg/kg; Escherichia coli absent in 10 g, with Enterobacteriaceae, Salmonella and Cronobacter criteria for dried infant products. The Regulation applies from 18 August 2026; pectins and foods lawfully placed on the market before that date may be used or marketed until stocks are exhausted or until their date of minimum durability.
